slides.headline: Swiss watch exports / up 9.1%
slides.body: October 2026 · Fifth month of growth in a row. Source: FH.
slides.visual_job: Template A typographic cover (no press photo exists for statistics): MARKET tag, Oswald headline with champagne second line, wordmark top-left, handle top-right, source and SWIPE along the bottom

slides.headline: +9.1% · CHF 2.46 billion in one month
slides.body: Fifth month of growth in a row. January to October: close to CHF 22 billion, up 3.4% on 2025.
slides.visual_job: Template A number slide matching the kit sample: champagne +9.1% at 250px, smoke label, ivory Oswald headline, Inter body

slides.headline: Steel drove the growth
slides.body: Wristwatch value by material, Oct 2026 vs Oct 2025: Steel CHF 778.0m +11.2%; Gold-steel CHF 437.9m +28.3%; Other metals CHF 175.6m +31.0%; Precious metal CHF 859.2m +0.4%. 1.5 million watches exported, up 12.9%.
slides.visual_job: Ink panel table of four materials; steel change is the single champagne moment

slides.headline: US up, China down
slides.body: USA +60.8%, France +101.6%, Hong Kong +7.3%, UK +6.5%, Japan -2.1%, China -12.1%. FH: the US jump is a favourable base effect linked to tariffs (US Jan-Oct -0.1%). France is mainly re-exports; the EU grew 9.2%.
slides.visual_job: Ink panel table of the six main markets with CHF value and change; USA change in champagne; smoke footnotes for the US and France context

slides.headline: Exports are not sales
slides.body: Gold prices, a strong Swiss franc and US tariffs all weigh on margins, says the FH. Export growth alone is not the full picture. Next FH data: 17 December 2026.
slides.visual_job: Three short ivory lines in ink panels, FH quote attribution, next release date as the single champagne moment
